label: FP
reason: Both alerts are False Positives. Alert 1 (java/xss): The sink writes results.toString() to the response. results comes from queryForObject(sql). sql is constructed using bar. In doSomething(), bar is assigned "bob" because switchTarget is always 'B' (guess="ABC"). Thus param does not reach sql or results. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): The sink constructs sql using bar. bar is assigned "bob" in doSomething() due to the hardcoded switch target 'B'. Thus param does not reach sql. Both sinks receive safe constants.

evidence.note: doSomething method sets bar to constant "bob" because switchTarget is always 'B' (guess="ABC")
SQL injection sink uses bar, which is resolved to constant "bob", blocking param
XSS sink prints results derived from safe sql, param does not reach sink
